This Regular Second Appeal is filed by the appellant challenging the judgment and decree dated 10.04.2013 passed in R.A. No.339/2011 by the learned Fast Track Court, Hunsur, Mysuru District,
confirming the judgment and decree dated 12.08.2010 passed in O.S.No.120/2007 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Hunsur.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the trial Court.

The appellant is defendant No.2, respondent No.1 is the plaintiff and respondent Nos.2 to 5 are the defendant Nos.1, 4, 3 and 5.
3.
Plaintiff filed a suit for partition and separate possession of 1/3 share over the suit schedule properties.
It is the case of the plaintiff that, defendant No.1 - Smt.Mahadevamma and Sri K.M. Muddappa are the legal heirs of late Sri Mallappa.
Late Sri Mallappa, who was the original propositus, had three children namely Sri Appa Jappa, Sri Lingarajappa and Sri K.M.Muddappa.

Suit schedule properties are the ancestral properties of the plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 3.
Plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 3 were in joint possession and enjoyment of the same.
The Government issued a notification for acquisition, proceedings were initiates of the suit item No.3 property.
The acquisition proceedings were initiated in the name of defendant No.2 and defendant No.2 is attempting to take compensation amount as there is no proper division.
Plaintiff requested the defendants to effect partition and separate possession, but the defendants refused to effect partition.
Hence, cause of action arose for filing a suit for partition and separate possession.

Defendant No.2 filed written statement admitting the relationship with the plaintiff and the defendants and contended that there was a prior partition on 24.04.1968 in the presence of panchayathdars and list of the properties were prepared and three list of prepared properties were given to each one.
As per the list out of the suit item No.1, 20 guntas were given to the share of each of the member and husband of defendant No.1 and 1 acre was allotted to the share of defendant No.2.
Suit item No.2 is the self acquired property of defendant No.2.

The land measuring 3 acres 34 guntas of suit item No.3 was not included in the partition as it was kept for marriage expenses of defendant No.2 and 26 guntas was in possession of defendant No.2 and remaining land was acquired by the Government in Sy.No.89/2 measuring 2 acres 11 guntas and Sy.No.81/1 measuring 3 acres was the ancestral property of the defendants and acquired from the join family nucleus.

Sale Deed was executed in the name of defendant No.1 and other items in Sy.No.81/A measuring 1 acre 18 guntas and in NC: 2024:KHC:31494 Sy.No.80/1B measuring 80/1B were allotted to the share of defendant No.2.
Defendant No.2 had discharged the loan borrowed for the family.
Hence, the suit filed by the plaintiff is barred by limitation and prays to dismiss the suit.

5. The Trial Court, on the basis of the above said pleadings, framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that suit properties are ancestral and joint properties of himself and defendant No.1 and 2?

sentences.text: Whether the plaintiff proves that he has got right of 1/3rd share in the suit properties?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs as sought for by him?
4. Whether the defendant No.2 proves that the joint family properties were divided among himself, plaintiff and husband of defendant No.1 namely Appajappa under memorandum of partition on 24.04.1968?

Whether the defendant No.2 proves that land bearing Sy.No.77 measuring 3 acres 34 guntas was left to him towards his marriage expenses and hence the said property was not included in the said memorandum of partition?
6. Whether the defendant No.2 proves that guntas (Item No.2) is his self acquired property and land bearing 80/2 measuring1 acre 18 guntas is the self acquired property of his wife Sudha?

7. Whether the defendant No.2 proves that acres 11 guntas and Sy.No.81/1 measuring 3 acres were purchased out of the income of ancestral and joint family properties in the name of defendant No.1 Mahadevamma?

defendant No.1 requested the panchathdars to keep said properties in the name of defendant No.1 to meet the contingencies of his daughters?
9. Whether the defendant No.2 proves that the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties?
10. Whether the defendant No.1 proves that she is entitled for 1/3 share in the suit properties?
11. What order or decree?

Additional Issue:
"Whether the suit is bad for partial partition?
6. In order to prove the case of the plaintiff, the plaintiff examined himself as PW-1 and got marked 33 documents as Exs.P1 to P33.
In rebuttal, defendant No.2 examined as DW-1 and defendant No.1 examined as DW.2 and examined one witness as DW.3 and got marked 27 documents as Exs.D1 to D27.

sentences.text: 4 7. The trial Court after hearing both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence, partly decreed the suit of the plaintiff.

It is ordered and decreed that the plaintiff has got 5/16th share over item Nos.1, 3, 5 to 7 and item Nos.1 and 2 in item No.4 of the suit schedule properties and he is entitled for partition and separate possession by metes and bounds.
It is further ordered and decreed that defendant Nos.1 and 2 have got 5/16 share each over item Nos.1, 3 , 5 to 7 and item Nos.1 and 2 in item No.4 of the suit schedule properties.
Further it is ordered and decreed that defendant No.4 got 1/16th share over item Nos.1, 3, 5 to 7 and item Nos.2 and 3 in item No.4 of the suit schedule properties.

The Trial Court has dismissed the suit insofar as item Nos.2 and 3 in item No.4 of the suit schedule properties [1-18 guntas in Sy.No.80/3] and directed defendant No.3 to disburse the compensation amount in item No.7 as per the above ratio after expiry of the appeal period.
The prayer to award the mesne profit was rejected.
Defendant No.2 aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.120/2007 preferred an appeal in R.A.No.339/2011.

The First Appellate Court, after hearing the parties, has framed the following points for consideration:
"1.
Whether the I.A. No.2 filed under section 41 rule 27 CPC by the appellant/defendant No.2 is deserves to be allowed?
2. Whether the defendant No.2 prove that there was already a partition in respect of item No.1,3,5 to 7 and also in Sl.No. 1 and partition dated 24.04.1968 marked as Ex.D-1?

3. Whether the impugned judgment and decree under appeal passed by the lower court is illegal, capricious, arbitrary which call for interference of this court?
4. What order?"
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:31494 9. The First Appellate Court, on assessment of the oral and documentary evidence, dismissed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 10.04.2013 and confirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
Defendant No.2 being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in RA No.339/2011 has filed this Regular Second Appeal.
10. Heard learned counsels for the parties.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for defendant No.2 submits that defendant No.2 in order to prove that there was a prior partition has produced Ex.D.1 which discloses that there was a prior partition between the plaintiff and defendants and the suit filed by the plaintiff for partition and separate possession is not maintainable, unless the plaintiff challenges Ex.D.1.
He also submits that the finding recorded by the First Appellate Court that Ex.D.1 is an incomplete document is incorrect and that the parties have acted upon Ex.D.1.
He also submits that the said aspect was overlooked by the both the trial Court as well as the First Appellate Court and proceeded to pass the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:31494 impugned judgments.
He submits that the impugned judgments passed by both the trial Court as well as the First Appellate Court are arbitrary and erroneous.
Hence, on these grounds prays to allow the appeal.

12. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the defendant No.2.
13.
There is no dispute with regard to the relationship between the parties to the suit and also the nature of the suit schedule properties.

The defence of the defendants that there was a prior partition between the plaintiff and the defendants and a memorandum of partition came to be executed between the parties and the said memorandum of partition was marked as Ex.D.1.
On perusal of Ex.D.1, it does not disclose what are the properties which are allotted to the share of the respective parties.

Further it is the defense of the defendants that, as on the date of the partition dated 24.04.1968, memorandum of partition was got prepared 3 sets and handed over one set to the plaintiff and husband of - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:31494 defendant No.1 and also to defendant No.2.

Defendant No.2 has not produced any record to show that memorandum of palupatti was handed over to the plaintiff and husband of defendant No.1 and there are no pleadings to that effect in the written statement.

Defendant No.2 except producing Ex.D.1 has not led any independent evidence to establish that there was a prior partition on 24.04.1968 as alleged in the written statement as alleged in the written statement.
14. It is well established principals of law that mere marking of document does not dispense it's proof.
The plaintiff denied the execution of Ex.D.1 and the defendants have not examined any attesting witness to Ex.D.1 in order to prove contents and execution of Ex.D.1.

Both the trial Court as well as the First Appellate Court concurrently recorded the finding of the fact that the defendant No.2 has failed to prove the execution of Ex.D.1 and further defendant No.2 has not produced any document to show that on the basis of Ex.D.1 the names of the respective - 14 - Sri K M Muddappa vs Sri Lingarajappa @ Ningarajappa on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199604618/
6 NC: 2024:KHC:31494 parties were entered in the revenue records.

sentences.text: Hence, from the oral evidence of the parties, it discloses that the parties have not acted upon Ex.D.1.

The trial Court and the First Appellate Court were justified in discarding the defence of the defendants in regard to the prior partition and the trial Court has rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiff.
The First Appellate Court on reassessment of the oral and documentary evidence rightly confirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
Hence, I do not find any substantial question of law that arises for consideration in this appeal and any error in the impugned judgments.

15. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
[a] The appeal is dismissed.
The Judgment and decree dated 10.04.2013 passed in R.A. No.339/2011 by the Fast Track Court, Hunsur, Mysuru District is confirmed.
[b] In view of dismissal of the appeal, I.A. No.1/2016 does not survive for consideration and hence dismissed.
[c] No order as to costs.
